prize_parts.citation: for the invention and development of optical lattice clocks, in which atoms trapped at a magic wavelength made possible measurements of time and frequency at the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: I keep B047 with Katori and Ye as my final position. Round 1 sharpened what the case rests on. The magic-wavelength lattice is a new physical principle for neutral atoms: it removes the trade-off between long interrogation time and trap-induced shifts, and no earlier prize rewarded it. Frequency combs (2005) supplied the ruler and ion control (2012) a different clock architecture. The result is not a single-group claim. JILA, RIKEN and Tokyo, PTB, NIST and SYRTE reproduce and cross-compare lattice clocks near 1e-18, which answers my usual question about independent confirmation and systematics better than any other shortlisted item except possibly B006. The credit is traceable: Katori for the scheme and the first strontium lattice clock, Ye for the accuracy, coherence and many-body control that set the records. The physics is not limited to metrology: millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, bounds on drifting constants and ultralight dark matter are measurements of nature, and the citation can rest on the lattice concept and its demonstrated accuracy without waiting for the redefinition of the second. That redefinition follows from this work and is not a precondition for crediting it.
statement.case_against: My position has real weaknesses. Four colleagues (Danielsson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson) see the clock as a tool, and the fundamental-physics output so far consists of limits, not a signal. A sceptic can still read it as a very successful sequel to 2005 and 2012, and the second has not yet been redefined. Support is narrower than for B006, which was ranked by seven members. The two-name cut leaves out the Yb and SYRTE groups, and I cannot prove from the supplied material that nobody there has a priority claim. I am also the chair and a supporter of this configuration, so my reading of the questions should be discounted accordingly. If the committee decides that a discovery of a new phase of matter outweighs a new measurement capability, B006 is the serious alternative, provided its third seat is resolved.

responses.point: The two-name cut is defensible because the decisive contributions are traceable, Katori for the scheme and first lattice clock and Ye for the accuracy and coherence frontier, and nearly every laboratory can check the number, which makes B047 more mature than IceCube.
responses.response: I agree, and your point about checkability is the one that decided my move away from B048. I accept your caution on priority: the Yb and SYRTE groups made real contributions, but I do not see a decisive third contribution that would justify a third name, and adding one would invite a priority dispute that the clean two-name credit avoids. I would write the citation around the lattice concept and its accuracy, as you propose, so that the 2005 and 2012 prizes are not repeated.

responses.point: The magic-wavelength idea is a new physical principle for neutral atoms and not a better comb or ion trap, but the novelty objection is the hardest one, and the citation might be centred on millimetre-scale relativistic redshift.
responses.response: Thank you for answering the question I put to you. I would not centre the citation on the redshift, because the redshift measurement is a consequence of the accuracy and is better kept as an example than as the achievement. A citation tied to the lattice concept and the 10^-18 accuracy is more durable if a later ion clock or a nuclear clock overtakes the numbers. I also agree that we should not insist that the second be redefined first. On your point about KM3NeT, I accept that B048 is less mature than I thought; I am keeping it only as an alternative.

responses.point: B006 is the cleanest case of a sharp prediction confirmed by experiment, with the Kane-Mele and Molenkamp loop closed and Mele moved into the trio in place of Hasan, though the HgTe credit gap remains.
responses.response: I agree that this is the most mature condensed-matter case and I still list B006 as my first alternative. Your move to Mele makes the 2D story cleaner but leaves the 3D ARPES discovery without a credited name, whereas Danielsson and Olsson keep Hasan and split Kane from Mele. Neither cut is wrong, which is precisely why I cannot yet call B006 the consensus choice. I am an experimentalist outside this field, so I rely on you and Olsson for the 2005 papers. Would a citation limited to the quantum spin Hall effect and its HgTe observation, with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, close the gap as you suggest, and would you accept that wording if the committee preferred B006?

responses.point: The committee should not settle on a trio only because ballots converge on it, B006 needs a check of what Mele contributed in the 2005 papers, and the clock is something you would rank above B038 or B022.
responses.response: I agree that convergence of ballots is not evidence, and that applies equally to my own position: the three of us who prefer B047 largely repeat each other's arguments. Your point that 2016 addressed phase transitions in model systems and not time-reversal-invariant topology in real materials seems strong to me, although I cannot judge it from within the field. If you can establish what Mele added in the 2005 papers, that would move B006 closer to my own ranking, since the attribution problem is the only reason I rank it second. I am glad that you rank the clock above circuit QED, and I would ask you to state which of the two reservations, novelty or the missing redefinition, decides your remaining distance from B047.

responses.point: Circuit QED opened the strong-coupling regime for microwave photons, reproduced in dozens of laboratories for twenty years, and is distinct from the 2025 prize, with disclosure of your conflict as director of WACQT.
responses.response: I appreciate the disclosure and I will not treat B038 as less than it is. It is a mature field and I see it as a first-rate candidate on the science. My remaining problem is the attribution: Girvin and Huang co-authored the 2004 proposal and the Yale experiment is a collective effort, so three names cannot cover it cleanly. The 2025 prize for circuits is also not neutral for a committee that must explain itself to the public. I would hold B038 for a later year and I have not placed it among my alternatives.

responses.point: The clock is an instrument rather than a discovery until the second is redefined or a signal appears, and IceCube source identification rests on very few objects.
responses.response: I accept the IceCube point completely and it is why I have moved B048 down. On the clock, I do not accept that discovery requires a signal. The lattice clock shows that neutral atoms in a magic-wavelength trap can be held with no motional or light-shift error to 1e-18, which nobody expected before 2001, and the millimetre-scale redshift measurement is a direct observation. Detectors and instruments that open a new observational window have been honoured before, and I treat this as a comparable case. I do see that this is a difference of philosophy between us and not a fact we can settle, so I will not claim that the clock must be preferred.

uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers B006, with the widest ballot support and about twenty years of confirmation but an unresolved third seat (Hasan or Mele), over B047, with narrower support but a clean two-name credit.

Whether four members who regard the lattice clock as a refinement of metrology can be persuaded that the magic-wavelength principle is a distinct discovery, and I cannot guarantee that the citation wording fully answers the 2005 and 2012 overlap.
Whether a third lattice-clock contributor from SYRTE or the Yb groups has a priority claim that I have not verified from the supplied material.
Whether IceCube source identifications will mature through KM3NeT or further neutrino observations, which affects whether B048 should wait another cycle; I do not claim it is ready now.
I cannot independently assess the condensed-matter credit questions (Mele versus Hasan, the HgTe proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang) and rely on colleagues and expert reviewers.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict is apparent for B047, B006 or B048 beyond what I disclosed in round 1. My PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations are unconnected to lattice clocks or topological insulators. IceCube (B048) lies in my own astroparticle field and I disclose that closeness since I list it as an alternative. As chair I also disclose that I support one of the two leading positions, and the committee should discount my chair summary accordingly.
